note: Review pressed through the future-maintainer angle. The dominant fact: the last revision's ten blind search/replace patches have physically corrupted the artifact — the entire plan is duplicated inside itself, splitting a load-bearing table in half. Several substantive spec gaps also survive underneath the corruption.

findings.section: whole document (visible mid-Phase 4, launch-surface table item 2)
findings.criterion: 1 launch-surface table — the "nothing left for Stage 2 to enumerate" exhaustive spawner enumeration the plan stakes its swarm-capture claim on. A future maintainer (or the Foreman Stage-2 consumer, which parses this document) cannot tell which copy is authoritative, whether the two copies diverge, or what item 2's full wiring statement actually says. The changelog ("Applied a search/replace patch" ×10, zero semantic content) confirms the reviser patched blind and never re-read the assembled artifact. This is not a formatting nit: the plan document IS the deliverable, and as written it is unshippable. Deduplicate, restore item 2 to one intact sentence, and diff the two copies to prove no divergent edits were stranded in the dead copy.
findings.message: The draft contains a complete second copy of itself embedded mid-sentence. Phase 4's launch-surface table item 2 reads "…envelope-measured today (real `# Master Plan (draft)" — and then the ENTIRE document (North Star, Phases 0–3) repeats, before the original sentence resumes hundreds of lines later with ", stays distinct per Stage-0 decision 3)". findings.section: all phase headings vs in-body references
findings.message: Every heading carries two numbers ("Phase 7 — Phase 6 — Historical backfill") while every in-body cross-reference uses only the inner one ("the Phase 6 backfill tool", "the Phase-2-tested munging function", "the Phase-1 claim path"). "Phase 6" therefore names the Surfaces phase by heading and the Backfill phase by reference — in the same document. The backfill/snapshot contract (criterion 4) is held together entirely by these cross-references ("Phase 6 reads the Phase-0 archive… using the Phase-2 munging function"), so a maintainer or Stage-2 wave-mapper resolving them against the headings wires the wrong dependencies. Pick ONE numbering, renumber every heading and every reference, and add a criterion→phase map so the resolution is mechanical.

findings.topic: closed vocabulary omits the intake failure mode
findings.section: Phase 2 (CLOSED provenance vocabulary) vs Phase 1 repair path
findings.criterion: 3 — The latch cannot be burned hermetically
findings.message: The frozen `usage_state` vocabulary excludes `sidecar-root-unavailable` — yet that state demonstrably exists on disk (3 intake records), the Phase-1 repair script's precondition check must RECOGNIZE it ("verify the current state is still `sidecar-root-unavailable`"), and, worse, the plan never defines what a BEACONED finalize emits when the sidecar root or the session's sidecar file is missing at finalize time — the exact failure mode that caused the intake poisoning. Does it defer? Emit `unmeasured`? Consume the claim? The conformance test asserting "no writer ever emits a value outside these sets" will either fail against reality or force an ad-hoc, untested state back in — vocabulary drift by emergency, the precise accretion the freeze exists to prevent. Name the sidecar-missing-under-beacon outcome explicitly (it should be non-CAS-consuming and retryable), and state whether legacy out-of-vocabulary states are reader-tolerated or migrated.

findings.criterion: 3 — The latch cannot be burned hermetically
findings.message: The plan claims to "invert the hermetic predicate from blocklist to positive identity," but the beacon mint condition is "exclusive bind on 8777 + the REAL un-redirected data dir" — and determining "un-redirected" is itself a blocklist check over redirect seams (is `ANCHOR_DATA_DIR` set?). The foresight brief names a SECOND seam the beacon predicate never consults: `ANCHOR_SIDECAR_DIR`, "the only hermetic escape." A manual-debug run on 8777 with the real data dir but a redirected sidecar root mints a valid beacon, is admitted to the CAS, reads the wrong (empty) sidecar root, and consumes the claim — recreating the poison class criterion 3 exists to kill, through the front door of the trust model. Either the beacon mint must refuse when ANY redirect seam is active (and the plan must maintain that seam list as new seams are added — say so, so a future maintainer adding a seam knows to touch the beacon), or a beaconed finalize that cannot locate the sidecar must be non-CAS-consuming per Finding 3. The "no supervisor enumeration to get wrong" boast is overstated; it traded supervisor enumeration for seam enumeration and didn't write the seam list down.

findings.topic: eager skill-layer finalize structurally forbidden by own trust model
findings.section: Phase 3 (launch-surface table tier 5, deferred items) vs Phase 1 trust model
findings.message: Stage-0 decision 4 locks "BOTH eager owner finalize + reconcile-dead catch-all." But under the Phase-1 trust model, only the beaconed server process may consume the CAS — and the agy-dispatch orchestrator is a separate CLI process that can never hold the beacon. The plan's own deferred item ("eager IN-PROCESS finalize inside the agy-dispatch skill itself") is therefore structurally impossible as named: a future maintainer who picks up that deferred task will build it, watch the beacon refuse admission on every call, and have to invent an unplanned workaround (a service finalize endpoint? beacon delegation?) at the highest-risk primitive. For the entire skill-layer swarm — 106 of 111 registry sessions, the population criterion 1 exists for — "eager owner finalize" quietly degrades to "sweep-only, up to ~30 minutes late," which is fine but is a MATERIAL narrowing of a locked decision that the plan should state honestly rather than defer as if it were buildable. Either specify the mechanism (e.g. the orchestrator POSTs a finalize request to the beaconed service, which performs the admitted write) or amend the deferred item to say sweep-is-the-owner for skill-layer sessions, permanently.

findings.criterion: 3 — a later live finalize can still measure (and 6, honest counting)
findings.message: `finalize-deferred` is retryable forever: the ~30-minute sweep "RETR[ies] every finalize-deferred record" with no exit condition, and the healthcheck WARNs "when live-registry sessions accumulate deferrals." A session whose sidecar never existed (or was pruned pre-capture) will defer on every sweep until the end of time — the deferred count only grows, and the yellow WARN becomes permanent wallpaper. The plan itself pins the locked severity rule's rationale: "a false alarm just trains the eye to ignore the banner." A permanently-yellow WARN is the same hazard one tier down. The vocabulary contains `unmeasured` but no transition rule deferred→unmeasured is defined anywhere — a future maintainer inherits an unbounded retry queue with no policy for declaring a session honestly unmeasurable. Define the terminality rule (e.g. N sweeps or sidecar-provably-absent ⇒ `unmeasured`, terminal, non-CAS-consuming... or explicitly "deferred is forever, WARN only above a delta threshold") — either is defensible; silence is not.

The sweep's stated trigger is "sidecars whose DIRNAME embeds a valid session marker but has no registry row" — but the dirname is keyed to a CWD, and the sweep's explicit target population (tier-b skill-layer spawns that bypass the wrapper, i.e. a skill invoking raw `claude` from inside a parent session's worktree) produces exactly the collision case: MULTIPLE session JSONL files inside ONE dirname that embeds the PARENT's session id. Does the sweep mint one record per dir (silently summing sub-agents into the parent)? One per JSONL file (against what session id — they have engine UUIDs, no registry rows)? Skip as ambiguous (silently dropping the very spend the tier-b catch-all promises to catch)? The plan specifies dirname↔id correlation for the ONE-file-per-dir case and says nothing about N-files-per-dir, which is the dominant bypass shape. Specify the attribution rule (parent-attribution with a `via-parent-worktree` provenance note would be honest) — otherwise "never invisible" is asserted, not designed.

findings.criterion: 3 — The latch cannot be burned hermetically
findings.message: "Truncated tail → `usage_state: measured-partial`, never a clean-looking number" — but does writing a measured-partial record CONSUME the exclusive-create claim? If yes, a transiently-truncated sidecar (AV lock, partial flush that the N-second mtime window happened to miss) permanently latches an undercount that append-only forbids ever correcting — a burned-latch variant in miniature. If no, what stops every subsequent sweep from re-reading and re-emitting? The claim-file semantics are defined for measured/deferred but not for partial. One sentence fixes it (e.g. partial consumes the claim ONLY after quiesce confirms the file can no longer grow — process provably dead — else defer).

findings.topic: snapshot read-only protection ineffective on Windows
findings.message: "Mark the archive read-only (attrib +R / ACL)" — on Windows, `attrib +R` on a DIRECTORY does not prevent creation, modification, or deletion of files within it; it is cosmetically meaningless for the stated goal. Only a deny-write ACL actually freezes the archive, and the plan offers the two as interchangeable ("attrib +R / ACL"). A future maintainer will take the cheap option and believe the snapshot is immutable when it isn't — undermining the "frozen snapshot" premise every backfill guarantee is anchored to. Also, "the disk cost is bounded" is asserted with no number: 55+ dirs of full JSONL transcripts for multi-million-token sessions plausibly runs to gigabytes; state the measured size before committing to copy-everything, or the Phase-0 operator discovers it mid-copy. Specify: deny-write ACL (not attrib), and record the actual byte total in the plan once measured.

findings.criterion: all (document fidelity to the locked North Star)
findings.message: The draft embeds the North Star verbatim (correct) and then immediately restates a paraphrased six-bullet "Success criteria" list. Two renderings of the locked criteria in one artifact invite drift — the paraphrase already compresses nuance (e.g. criterion 1's "where wired" qualifier, load-bearing per Finding 5, is dropped from the bullet). Delete the paraphrase; the verbatim block is the only copy that should exist.
